title: Personal Checking: Source Savings Eligibility Behind an Overdraft Protection Transfer Fee
content:
## Principle

A Personal Checking overdraft protection transfer may only draw on a savings account whose savings tier the Savings & Money Market Accounts terms designate as an eligible overdraft protection source. A transfer fee arising from a transfer that drew on a savings account of any other tier was charged in error.

## Which fee, which transfer, which savings account

- **The fee examined** is the overdraft protection transfer fee most recently posted to the checking account. Transfer fees posted before it are dealt with under the general Personal Checking fee refund rules, not here.
- **The transfer behind it** is the entry the fee names as its source.
- **The savings account that funded it** is the account that transfer entry names as the other PCB account on the transfer.
- **Its eligibility** is read from the tier of that savings account, as the savings terms define it for that tier.

## Judgement

| Funding savings account | Eligibility of its tier | Finding on this ground |
|---|---|---|
| found on the customer's record | not eligible | the fee is a bank error |
| found on the customer's record | eligible | no bank error on this ground |
| not on the customer's record | cannot be established | no finding on this ground |

Where the funding savings account cannot be found on the customer's record, its eligibility cannot be shown either way, so this ground neither condemns nor clears the fee.

## Tracing illustration (hypothetical references)

The latest transfer fee, entry F-7, names transfer T-3 as its source. Transfer T-3 names savings account S-9 as the other account. S-9 is held in a savings tier that the savings terms do not mark as eligible. Finding: fee F-7 was charged in error on this ground. Had T-3 named a savings account held in an eligible tier, this ground would give no error.
